title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: supply of sufficient grace does not exclude antecedent reprobation — preparation of efficacious grace does, and implies election
pass_a_gloss: If Arminius, Corvinus, and their assenterers will grant us even this, it will follow that the supplying of sufficient grace does not exclude antecedent reprobation, but that the preparation of efficacious grace does in truth exclude it, and brings in election. Let it therefore be taken, that sufficient grace is administered by God unto all adults, yet (as you see) even with a Jesuit as judge, it does not thence follow that they were not reprobated before the foresight of final demerits.
pass_b_english: If Arminius, Corvinus, and their backers grant us even that much, it follows that supplying sufficient grace does not shut out antecedent reprobation — whereas preparing efficacious grace truly does shut it out, and brings election in. So grant that God administers sufficient grace to every adult: still (as you see), even by a Jesuit's judgment, it does not follow they were not reprobated before foresight of final demerits.
source_text: Si Arminius, Corvinus, eorumque assipulatores vel hoc nobis concesserint, sequetur sufficientis gratiae suppeditationem non excludere antecedaneam reprobationem, sed efficacis gratiae praeparationem revera illam excludere, et electionem inferre. Sumatur igitur, omnibus adultis gratiam sufficientem a Deo administrari, tamen (uti videtis) vel Jesuita judice, non inde sequitur eos non fuisse ante praevisionem finalium demeritorum reprobatos.
